content:
amanda: Quick follow-up to the multi-region RFC — summary and open questions.

amanda: TL;DR: We want region-local primary per-account to meet residency + active-active read routing for global customers. Thoughts on cross-region replication strategy and failover semantics?

raj: +1 on region-local primary for residency. For failover we can do async replication with change streams and per-tenant WAL. RPO won't be 0 but it's predictable.

lucas: Concern: async replication means split-brain risk during network partition. How do we handle concurrent writes? Do we require a single write-path (write-to-primary only) and reject others?

emily: For most apps write-to-primary is fine. Enterprise customers who need RPO=0 can opt into sync replication (higher latency/cost). We should expose a per-tenant policy.

raj: Agreed. Implementation sketch:
```
routing.policy: "geo-primary"
tenant.mapping: { "eu-*": "eu-west-1", "us-*": "us-east-1" }
replication.mode: { "default": "async", "enterprise": "sync" }
```
Also store primary-region in config-service + global-control-plane for routing.

amanda: Good. Two more things: cache/KV warming and model serving state. If we failover region, KV cache gets cold -> latency spike. We need fast prefix cache warmup or keep hot-standby for heavy tenants.

lucas: For model runtimes, we can't afford cross-region KV fetch per-token. Keep model-serving state local. For failover, rebuild cache from persisted checkpoints (small, incremental) and consider staged warmup.

emily: Operationally we should also add an automated traffic-shift playbook: - mark tenant as degraded - dry-run traffic shift - promote replica in target region - rollback hook. Capture in Console as a button.

raj: Regarding leader election: prefer using existing control-plane (etcd/consul) and a lease timestamp. Avoid complex consensus in the data plane.

amanda: Action items: 1) Raj & Lucas to draft implementation RFC for geo-primary + replication modes (due EOW). 2) Emily to prototype Console traffic-shift UX. 3) Ops to author runbook for failover and cold-cache mitigation.

deploy-bot: rfc/multi-region-geo-primary v0.1 deployed to staging :white_check_mark:

amanda: Thanks — let's keep the decision lean: default async geo-primary, per-tenant sync opt-in, explicit failover runbook. Will post a short RFC update with the decision and rough API surface.

lucas: One last note — add metrics: cross-region replication lag, failover time, cache-warmup latency. We'll need these for SLOs.

emily: +1

amanda: End.
